{{Quote|Whisper all you like! La la la. They gave me a palace on Alsakan / I'd prefer a ditch on Alderaan.|A delirious Republic excavator, [[Lefry Kaonai]], sings a tune|<ref name="Star Wars: The Old Republic">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''</ref>}}
'''Alsakan''' was an [[Ecumenopolis/Legends|ecumenopolis]] [[Planet/Legends|world]] in the [[Alsakan system/Legends|Alsakan system]] in the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]]. A [[Core Founder/Legends|Core Founder]] on the [[Perlemian Trade Route/Legends|Perlemian Trade Route]], Alsakan was an ancient, wealthy world that had been a major political player for centuries, and was responsible for the seventeen [[Alsakan Conflicts/Legends|Alsakan Conflicts]] that had been [[Coruscant of the Outer Rim|fought]] with [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] over the nature and shape of the early [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]].

==Description==
Positioned on the [[Perlemian Trade Route/Legends|Perlemian Trade Route]] immediately Rimward of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], Alsakan was a heavily-[[City/Legends|urbanized]] planet that had been a regional power broker for millennia.<ref name="TEA" /> A [[Core Founder/Legends|Core Founder]], it was considered part of the [[Arrowhead]], the triangle of ancient systems at the head of the Perlemian and the [[Corellian Run/Legends|Corellian Run]] that had grown out of the [[Tetrahedron]] in the earliest days of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]].<ref name="TEA" />

Alsakani culture and values came to dominate the [[Human/Legends|Human]]-majority worlds of the Perlemian, which championed local independence and limited government. This region, known as "the Axis", came into opposition to the heavily-urbanized and bureaucratic megaworlds of "[[the Spin]]," the parts of the Corellian Run and [[Metellos Trade Route/Legends|Metellos Trade Route]] dominated by Coruscant where a strong state was seen as a protector against economic exploitation. Over a period of 14,000 years, from [[17,000 BBY]] to [[3017 BBY]], the two coalitions would fight [[Alsakan Conflicts/Legends|seventeen wars]] over these ideological differences.<ref name="Warfare" />

A wealthy planet, at the start of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], Alsakan was able to afford one of the earliest [[Star Dreadnought/Legends|Star Dreadnoughts]] for the [[Alsaka sector/Legends|Alsaka sector's]] [[Planetary Security Forces|local defense forces]].<ref name="Warfare" /> [[Xenvaer]] was a city on Alsakan.<ref name="HoloNet News 53">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|53|news/13425_4.html|RRM Fundraiser a Huge Success}}</ref> [[Archais (kingdom)|Archais]] was an ancient region of Alsakan, and [[Rucapar]] one of its major cities. Built among five equidistant mountains, Rucapar had been the site of the [[Alsakan Mosaics]], an ancient [[Twenty Wonders of the Galaxy|Wonder of the Galaxy]] that stretched in five lanes of tiles to each mountain. The city and the mosaics were largely destroyed during the [[Cleansing of Rucapar]] in the [[Third Alsakan Conflict]].<ref name="Warfare" /><ref name="TEA" />

==History==
===Early history===
Alsakan was once a [[Killik/Legends|Killik]] colony before [[30,000 BBY]] when they were taken to the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]], possibly by the [[Celestial/Legends|Celestials]].<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Alien Species" /> At least [[Unidentified Killik Sith warrior|one Killik]] from Alsakan became a user of the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] and was able to escape the world and flee to [[Sarafur]].<ref name="Race for the Tessent" /> Alsakan later became a world of the [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Rakata Empire]].<ref name="TEA" />

In [[26,000 BBY/Legends|26,000 BBY]] Alsakan was colonized by Humans from Coruscant in the colony ship ''[[Kuat Explorer]]''.<ref name="Han Solo and the Corporate Sector Sourcebook">''[[Han Solo and the Corporate Sector Sourcebook]]''</ref> The [[Planet/Legends|planet]] was divided into many kingdoms until the King of Archais united the planet after the [[Battle of the Ten Valleys]].<ref name="Race for the Tessent" /> Alsakan became a Core Founder of the Galactic Republic in [[25,053 BBY]].<ref name="TEA" /> The Alsakani had favored a limited economic and political union over the galaxy-spanning state the Galactic Republic became, and for many centuries afterwards were inclined to see the Republic government as overly-powerful.<ref name="Warfare" /> In particular, Alsakan was isolated from the cultural and economic pressures that produced [[Old Galactic Standard]], the [[Trade language/Legends|trade language]] that became [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Galactic Basic]], and the Alsakani continued to speak [[High Galactic (language)|High Galactic]].<ref name="Written Word" />

During the [[Tionese War]], Alsakan suffered heavy destruction from [[pressure bomb]]s released by warships of the [[Honorable Union of Desevro and Tion|Honorable Union of Desevro & Tion]].<ref name="Warfare" /> The planet served as a temporary [[Tionese (group)/Legends|Tionese]] forward base for their [[Battle of Coruscant (Tionese War)|raids against Coruscant]], and the significant Tionese cultural influence led the Alsakani to adopt a number of characters from the [[Tionese/Legends|Tionese alphabet]] to create a [[High Galactic/Legends|new writing system]] for High Galactic.<ref name="Written Word" />

===The Alsakan Conflicts===
Amid growing economic competition between the Core Worlds to sponsor colonization throughout the [[Great Manifest Period/Legends|Great Manifest Period]], Alsakan became the champion of the Human-dominated worlds of the Perlemian Trade Route. The coalition along the Perlemian led by Alsakan became known as "the Axis", and [[Coruscant of the Outer Rim|envied]] Coruscant's predominance of the urban, multispecies worlds of the Corellian Run and the Metellos Trade Route. Coruscant's coalition, known the "the Spin", viewed a strong, centralized state as a protector against economic exploitation and inequality, while Alsakan and the Axis were aristocratic in their values, enthusiastic for open spaces and local independence.<ref name="Warfare" />

From 17,000 BBY until 3017 BBY,<ref name="TEA" /> Alsakan tried to usurp Coruscant's predominance seventeen times, causing the Alsakan Conflicts between the planets' holdings in the [[Expansion Region/Legends|Expansion Region]].<ref name="The New Essential Chronology">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> The [[First Alsakan Conflict]] began when Alsakani younger sons, assisted by other noble families like [[House Juoni]] of [[Kaikielius/Legends|Kaikielius]], moved to claim systems in the path of the Spin-based [[Grand Companies]]. The Republic backed the Grand Companies, and though the first conflict was resolved with the [[Challat Compromise]], Alsakan continued to sponsor colonization across [[The Slice/Legends|the Slice]] in the path of the Grand Companies. The [[Second Alsakan Conflict]] began in [[16,200 BBY]], and the Conflicts soon fell into a pattern: Alsakani nobles and Coruscant-backed megacorps fought for resources in the Expansion Region, while the [[Corellian Hegemony]] declared neutrality and protected its own interests. While both Coruscant and Alsakan were raided, neither had the resources to split their forces between attack and defense.<ref name="Warfare" /><ref name="Praji">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/source/praji/20090205.html|text=Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji|int=Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji}}</ref> However, Alsakan did suffer severe damage during the Third Alsakan Conflict, when the city of Rucapar was largely destroyed along with the ancient Alsakan Mosaics.<ref name="TEA" />

[[File:FifthAlsakanConflict.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Admiral [[Hirken]]'s defense of Alsakani colonies in the [[Northern Dependencies/Legends|Northern Dependencies]] during the [[Fifth Alsakan Conflict]].]]
The Alsakan Conflicts saw a number of military innovations, including Alsakan's [[Atgeir-class battlecruiser|''Atgeir''-class battlecruiser]]. The [[Seventeenth Alsakan Conflict]] saw the introduction into the Republic fleet of the [[Invincible-class Dreadnaught Heavy Cruiser|''Invincible''-class Dreadnaught Heavy Cruiser]], in opposition to the [[Axis sublight missile corvette]].<ref name="Han Solo and the Corporate Sector Sourcebook" />

After the Republic fell under the control of the [[Pius Dea]] cult in [[11,987 BBY]], it launched a series of increasingly-violent [[Pius Dea Crusades|crusades]] against the species of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]]. In response, Alsakan and much of the Axis seceded from the Republic around [[11,820 BBY]]. The [[Sixth Alsakan Conflict]] was a vicious war between Alsakan and the Pius Dea Republic, which saw Alsakan open up secret lines of communication with numerous species that had been the victims of the Crusades, including the [[Duros/Legends|Duros]], [[Herglic/Legends|Herglics]] and [[Hutt/Legends|Hutts]]. These alliances were instrumental to the ultimate fall of the Pius Dea in [[10,967 BBY]], where Pius Dea [[Renunciates]], backed by the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] and Alsakani battleships, helped destroy Pius Dea forces in the [[Seventh Alsakan Conflict]], culminating in the cult's ultimate defeat at the [[Battle of Uquine]].<ref name="Warfare" />

Eventually, the Alsakan Conflicts grew less brutal, with longer stretches of peace, until after [[8000 BBY]] they were considered minor diversions. The Seventeenth and final Alsakan Conflict was sparked in 3017 BBY by Alsakan maintaining and expanding its fleet despite the conclusion of the [[Galactic War]]s. The Republic responded by building a fleet of two-kilometer-long ''Invincible''-class fast battleships. Alsakan and the Axis' response was mass-produced squadrons of sublight missile corvettes, which successfully defended their systems from Republic raids. However, [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]] reacted with a fleet of long-range frigates. Technological breakthroughs enabled them to be outfitted with fast engines, strong shields, and heavy turbolasers, allowing [[Prince-Admiral/Legends|Prince-Admiral]] [[Jonash e Solo]] to rapidly outfight both Coruscanti and Alsakani battleships. Coruscant and Alsakan responded by declaring war on Corellia, but both were decisively defeated and were forced to accept a [[Alsakan Conflicts peace treaty|peace treaty]].<ref name="Warfare" />

A long-term result of the Conflicts was to make colonization along the Perlemian Trade Route unattractive, resulting in a shift of colonists to the west of the Corellian Run and along the growing [[Corellian Trade Spine/Legends|Corellian Trade Spine]]. The Corellian Hegemony in the Expansion Region thrived at the expense of the Slice, attracting billions of colonists and seeing the development of the [[77 Sectors]] along the Run, a region that Corellia dominated as late as the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]].<ref name="TEA" />

===The Rise of the Empire===
[[File:Fird-TEA.jpg|thumb|left|150px|[[Fird]], [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] of Alsakan, who represented the planet around [[700 BBY]], during the debates on the [[Matter of Creating an Outer Expansion Zone]].]]
In [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]], the [[Alsakan Tessent]] was carved to commemorate the Battle of the Ten Valleys. Native [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] [[Jilst Bindalin]] stole the Tessent and took it to the tomb of the Killik darksider on Sarafur, whom Bindalin believed to have been a [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]].<ref name="Race for the Tessent" /> Around 700 BBY, Senator Fird served as Alsakan's delegate to the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]], and he participated in the debates on the Matter of Creating an Outer Expansion Zone, noting the disadvantages of both centrally-directed colonization and undirected, independent local efforts of settlement.<ref name="TEA" />

In 22 BBY, the [[Mothers United March]] was held in response to the [["Baby Ludi" custody case]] on Alsakan,<ref name="HoloNet News 50">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|50|jediwatch/1344_1.html|Jedi Vs. The Force of a Mother's Love}}</ref> as was a [[Refugee Relief Movement/Legends|Refugee Relief Movement]] fundraiser.<ref name="HoloNet News 53" />

Alsakan remained loyal to the Galactic Republic during the Clone Wars, and its Star Dreadnought was put into service with the [[Republic Navy/Legends|Republic Navy]] to defend the Core against Separatist incursions.<ref name="Warfare" /> After the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy's]] [[Bulwark Fleet]] [[Battle of Foerost (Clone Wars)|broke through]] the Republic's [[Foerost Siege|siege]] of [[Foerost/Legends|Foerost]], a [[Battle of Alsakan (Clone Wars)|battle]] took place above Alsakan as the Republic's [[Victory Fleet]] [[Foerost campaign|chased]] the Separatists throughout the Core Worlds.<ref name="The New Essential Chronology" />

===The Galactic Civil War and beyond===
While a member of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], Alsakan was one of the first Imperial worlds to surrender to [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Gial Ackbar/Legends|Gial Ackbar's]] fleet as the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] entered the Core Worlds in [[6 ABY/Legends|6 ABY]].<ref name="Dark Empire Sourcebook">''[[Dark Empire Sourcebook]]''</ref> In [[10 ABY/Legends|10 ABY]], however, the forces of the [[Palpatine/Legends|Reborn Emperor Palpatine]] [[Pre–Shadow Hand campaign|advanced]] out of the [[Deep Core/Legends|Deep Core]] and reconquered numerous Core Worlds, [[Battle of Alsakan (Galactic Civil War)|including Alsakan]]. After Imperial forces collapsed into infighting during the [[Imperial Civil War]], rival factions [[Battle above Alsakan|clashed again]] over the planet, resulting in the mutual destruction of the Star Dreadnoughts ''[[Whelm]]'' and ''[[Panthac]]''.<ref name="Warfare" /><ref name="TEA" />

In [[23 ABY/Legends|23 ABY]], the Alsakan Tessent was at last recovered in the [[Moddell sector/Legends|Moddell sector]].<ref name="Race for the Tessent" />

During the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], Alsakan capitulated to the [[Yuuzhan Vong|extragalactic invaders]], but was liberated by the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|Galactic Alliance]] after the war.<ref name="The New Jedi Order: The Unifying Force">''[[The New Jedi Order: The Unifying Force]]''</ref>

==Inhabitants==
The Alsakani were Human settlers who had arrived on the planet aboard the colony ship ''Kuat Explorer'' some twenty-six thousand years before the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]].<ref name="Han Solo and the Corporate Sector Sourcebook" /> As a people, they were aristocratic in their values and enthusiastic for open spaces and local independence. Consequently, they had sought a limited economic and political union when the Galactic Republic was formed, and for much of their history were inclined to see Coruscant as too powerful, resulting in the many Alsakan Conflicts.<ref name="Warfare" />

Reflecting their views, the ancient Alsakani national epic, the ''[[Archaiad]]'', described the Perlemian Trade Route as "an arrow sent into the possible". Seeking distance from authority, Alsakan's younger sons established small colonies in the [[Inner Rim/Legends|Inner Rim]], and cared little for government bureaucracy or mass-produced goods beyond [[Warship/Legends|warships]] and [[Blaster/Legends|blasters]].<ref name="Warfare" />

For much of their early history, the Alsakani did not adopt Old Galactic Standard and continued to speak High Galactic. They were responsible for popularizing the High Galactic alphabet as an alternative to [[Aurebesh/Legends|Aurebesh]], as part of Alsakan's efforts to portray itself as an alternate galactic capital. The High Galactic script was created after the Alsakani combined [[Tionese/Legends|Tionese characters]] with others of their own invention, creating a distinctive new alphabet. Owing to Alsakan's values, High Galactic became a popular script among upper-class speakers of Galactic Basic, and its influence endured for millennia after the Alsakan Conflicts.<ref name="Written Word" />

The infamous outlaw [[Doctor/Legends|surgeon]] [[Cornelius Evazan/Legends|Doctor Cornelius Evazan]] was an Alsakani active in the Outer Rim during the Galactic Civil War, performing horrific experiments on unwitting captives.<ref name="Star Wars Character Encyclopedia">''[[Star Wars Character Encyclopedia]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
Alsakan was first mentioned as a Core World in [[1993]]'s ''[[Dark Empire Sourcebook]]''. ''[[Han Solo and the Corporate Sector Sourcebook]]'', released that same year, introduced the Alsakan Conflicts and the concept of Alsakan as an early challenger to Coruscant as the dominant power in the galaxy.<ref name="Han Solo and the Corporate Sector Sourcebook" /> The Alsakan Conflicts were additionally mentioned in [[2005]]'s ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''.<ref name="Dark Empire Sourcebook" /><ref name="The New Essential Chronology" />

The influence of the Alsakan Conflicts on the development of galactic colonization and settlement was established in [[2009]]'s ''[[The Essential Atlas]]''. The role of Alsakan in creating and disseminating the High Galactic alphabet as an alternative to Aurebesh during the Conflicts was developed in [[2010]]'s ''[[The Written Word]]'', a [[Hyperspace: The Official Star Wars Fan Club|''Hyperspace'']] article written to explain the various [[Writing/Legends|writing systems]] of the galaxy.<ref name="Written Word" />

The Conflicts, and Alsakani culture, were further fleshed out in [[2012]]'s ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'', which established Alsakan as a very different civilization to Coruscant.<ref name="Warfare" /><ref name="TEA" /> A concept ultimately not included in ''The Essential Guide to Warfare'' would have established Alsakan as having experienced significant influence from Tionese culture during the prolonged period of occupation during the Tionese War. This occupation was envisioned as having substantially influenced Alsakani culture and language, and inculcated a myth that the Alsakani were a lost Tionese colony.<ref name="Endnotes">{{Tumblr|subdomain=jasonfry|url=post/20907109370/eg-to-warfare-endnotes-pt-2|name=Jason Fry's Dorkery|text=EG to Warfare: Endnotes Pt. 2}}</ref>
